title: Heterologous Protein Expression in E. coli
author: Diep R R Ganguly
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bdjti4nn
materials: Buffer recipes Auto-induction TB medium (alternatively, liquid LB media for IPTG induction) 5 g/L yeast extract 20 g/L tryptone 85.5 mM NaCl (5 g/L) 22 mM KH 2 PO 4 (2.99 g/L) 42 mM Na 2 HPO 4 (5.96 g/L) Supplement fresh: 0.6% glycerol, 0.05% glucose, 0.2% lactose 10X PBS Dissolve the following in 800 mL H 2 O: 80 g of NaCl (1.37 M) 2.0 g of KCl (27 mM) 14.4 g of Na 2 HPO 4 (100 mM) 2.4 g of KH 2 PO 4 (18 mM) Adjust pH to 7.4. Add H 2 O to 1L. Autoclave Store 10X stock at 4 °C from which you can dilute 1:10 to make 1X working stock to keep at room temp. Make PBS-T by supplementing with 0.05 - 0.1% Tween20. Can replace with TBS-T http://cshprotocols.cshlp.org/content/2015/3/pdb.rec085670.full?text_only=true . Re-suspension buffer 50 mM Tris-HCl pH 8 2 mM EDTA Cell lysis buffer 50 mM NaH 2 PO 4 pH 8 (or ~1-2 pH units away from pI of expressed protein) 500 mM sodium chloride 10 mM imidazole 0.5% Triton X-100 10% glycerol 2 mM DTT ( add fresh before use) 1x Protease-inhibitor cocktail ( add fresh before use) Denaturing buffer 8 M Urea 4% CHAPS 35 mM Tris-HCl pH 8 Adjust pH to 7.5 if necessary for dissolving urea (or warm to 40 °C).

steps.title: Transform E. coli with plasmid
steps.instruction: Introduce the purified plasmid into the chosen E. coli strain using either electroporation or chemical competence.

substeps.instruction: Electroporation: thaw 50 µL electro‑competent cells on ice for 15 min, add 0.5–1 µL plasmid, flick to mix, transfer to a chilled cuvette without bubbles, dry cuvette exterior, keep on ice, set electroporator to 1.8 kV, 25 µF, 200–400 Ω, electroporate, immediately add 1 mL LB, transfer to a micro‑fuge tube using p1000 and p200 pipettes, recover at 37 °C, ~200 rpm for >1 h.

Chemical competence: thaw 50 µL chemically‑competent cells on ice for 15 min, add 0.5–1 µL plasmid, flick to mix, keep on ice 30 min, set water bath to 42 °C, heat‑shock 30–90 s (cell‑type dependent), return to ice 5 min, add 1 mL LB, recover at 37 °C, ~200 rpm for >1 h.

steps.title: Plate transformed cells on selective media
steps.instruction: Plate ~100 µL of the recovered transformation mixture onto selective LB agar and incubate overnight at 37 °C; adjust volume if needed to obtain isolated colonies.

steps.title: Pick colony and inoculate starter culture
steps.instruction: Pick a single colony and inoculate 3–5 mL of LB or TB medium containing the appropriate antibiotic; grow overnight at 37 °C with ~200–250 rpm shaking.

steps.title: Set up large expression culture
steps.instruction: Prepare the desired volume of expression medium (auto‑induction TB or LB for IPTG induction) in an aerated vessel; include a control lacking lactose or IPTG; inoculate at a 1:50 dilution (e.g., 1 mL starter into 49 mL medium).

steps.title: Induce protein expression
steps.instruction: For LB/IPTG: grow culture at 37 °C to OD₆₀₀ = 0.8, add 0.2–0.4 mM IPTG (keep an uninduced aliquot), then incubate overnight at the chosen temperature (18–25 °C). Verify that the uninduced culture’s OD₆₀₀ is ≥0.1 higher. For auto‑induction TB: grow overnight (>12 h) or until OD₆₀₀ = 2, sampling as desired.

steps.title: Harvest cells by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Pellet cultures at 4 °C, 7,000 rcf for 10 min; optionally remove a 1–3 mL aliquot and store at –20 °C for a quick expression test.

steps.title: Wash and snap‑freeze cell pellet
steps.instruction: Discard supernatant, wash the pellet with resuspension buffer, re‑pellet as above, discard wash, snap‑freeze the pellet in liquid N₂ and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Pellet cells at max speed
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the washed pellet at maximum speed for 3 min and remove the supernatant.

steps.title: Resuspend cells for crude lysate
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 100 µL 1× PBS per 1 mL of original culture (e.g., 100 µL for a 1 mL culture); store the crude lysate at –20 °C when not in use.

steps.title: Prepare sample buffer and calculate loading
steps.instruction: Add 4× LDS sample buffer, DTT to a final 50 mM, and MgCl₂ to a final 100 mM (prepare a mastermix if desired). Calculate loading volume using μL = [180/CF]/OD, where CF = culture volume / resuspension volume (e.g., CF = 10 for 1 mL → 100 µL).

steps.title: Heat and chill samples
steps.instruction: Heat the sample at 72 °C for 10 min, then place on ice for 5 min and spin at maximum speed for 15 min.

steps.title: Separate supernatant for SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Transfer the cleared supernatant to new tubes, avoiding any sticky DNA coating, and proceed to SDS‑PAGE or Western blot analysis.

steps.title: Run SDS‑PAGE or Western blot
steps.instruction: Load the prepared samples onto an SDS‑PAGE gel, stain with Coomassie, or transfer to a PVDF membrane for Western blot (use epitope tag if present).

steps.title: Prepare soluble protein lysate
steps.instruction: Resuspend the remaining cell pellet in lysis buffer whose pH is >1 unit away from the protein’s isoelectric point; keep the suspension on ice at all times.

steps.title: Sonicate cell suspension
steps.instruction: Transfer the suspension to a clean micro‑fuge tube (retain any excess at –20 °C) and sonicate with a Q125 ultrasonicator (125 W, 20 kHz, 60 % amplitude) for three 30‑second bursts on ice.

steps.title: Centrifuge to obtain soluble fraction
steps.instruction: Spin the sonicated lysate at 16,000 g for 30 min at 4 °C; collect the supernatant (soluble protein) and keep the pellet at –20 °C for insoluble fraction processing.

steps.title: Process insoluble fraction
steps.instruction: Resuspend the insoluble pellet in denaturing buffer, repeat sonication and centrifugation as above, and collect the resulting supernatant.

steps.title: Quantify protein by Bradford assay
steps.instruction: Determine protein concentrations of soluble and insoluble fractions using a Bradford assay; normalize each sample to the desired loading amount (e.g., 5 µg).

steps.title: Analyze fractions on SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Run the normalized soluble and insoluble samples on SDS‑PAGE, stain with Coomassie or perform Western blot to verify recombinant protein expression.
